bindings.label: Patient experienced blurred vision and progressive visual impairment in the affected eye

A 78-year-old woman underwent DMEK surgery; four weeks postoperatively, mild opacification in the graft-host interface was observed, visual acuity rehabilitation stopped at 20/50, graft was attached, and stromal thickness returned to normal (552 μm)

Six months later, the patient complained of blurred vision; physical examination revealed graft detachment caused by a paracentral opaque mass, enlargement of the abnormality, and pseudohypopyon formation
At 28 months follow-up, visual impairment had increased
Recurrence of primary corneal endothelial disease
Histology shows graft detachment by a cyst containing cellular debris, positive cytokeratin, and male donor origin
AS-OCT reveals hyperdensity at the graft detachment
Microbiological proof of infection is absent
Donor-derived epithelial cyst is the cause of graft detachment and pseudohypopyon
Progressive enlargement of the donor-derived epithelial cyst explains the delayed clinical worsening
